key_insight: A deep-learning surrogate can predict clinically relevant hemodynamic markers for intracranial aneurysms from patient geometry in real time, enabling CFD-level insights without the time and expertise burden of full simulations.
problem_solved: CFD-derived fluid-mechanical markers are valuable for assessing aneurysm risk but are too slow, specialized, and low-throughput for routine clinical use or large trials—this work provides a fast, automated alternative that works on realistic (non-idealized) patient geometries.
method: Generate training targets by running CFD on a diverse set of non-idealized, patient-derived aneurysm geometries to obtain hemodynamic markers.
Train a deep-learning surrogate model that maps 3D aneurysm morphology to biomechanical markers, optimized for runtime and robustness to realistic geometry artifacts.
Evaluate the surrogate against CFD on held-out cases for marker agreement and measure runtime speedups to demonstrate real-time inference capability.
impact: Enables scalable, real-time hemodynamic assessment for clinical workflows and trials; for ML practitioners it exemplifies building physics-informed surrogate models that trade minimal accuracy loss for large gains in speed and clinical applicability.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: patient imaging → geometry extraction → surrogate model → hemodynamic marker outputs (vs CFD baseline).
Side-by-side heatmaps on 3D aneurysm geometry: surrogate prediction vs CFD ground truth to show spatial agreement.
Bar chart: runtime comparison (CFD vs surrogate) and error metrics (MAE/RMSE) to illustrate speed/accuracy tradeoff.
Scatter plot: predicted vs CFD marker values across test cases with a line of identity to visualize calibration and bias.
paper_title: RHSIA: Real-time Hemodynamics Surrogation for Non-idealized Intracranial Aneurysms
paper_authors: Yiying Sheng, Wenhao Ding, Dylan Roi, Leonard Leong Litt Yeo, Hwa Liang Leo
